ordered_diagnoses: Fibrosing alopecia in a pattern distribution

s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, progressive, asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin lesion with localized hair loss on the scalp and forehead
salient_findings: Arc-shaped, depressed skin groove on the left side of the forehead, frontal scalp, and vertex area
Localized linear hair loss and hair thinning on the left scalp area
Dermoscopic examination revealed short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation
key_facts: The patient is a man in his 50s
The lesion began approximately 10 years earlier
The patient received 2 doses of intralesional steroid via injection on a small bald patch on the vertex
The lesion gradually progressed to the frontal scalp and eventually made a linear furrow on the left side of his forehead
The patient denied any trauma history
The patient had no history of connective tissue disease
No evidence of systemic involvement, such as arthralgia, photosensitivity, or skin rashes
Dermoscopic examination revealed several short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation
The result of a hair pull test was negative
Histopathologic examination showed predominant lymphocytic infiltrates in perifollicular and periappendageal regions of the dermis and lobular panniculitis
Direct immunofluorescence was positive with granular deposition of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, and fibrinogen in the dermal blood vessels

shortlist.label: Discoid lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Positive direct immunofluorescence and granular deposition of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, and fibrinogen in dermal blood vessels

shortlist.label: Lichen planopilaris
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic, progressive, asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin lesion with localized hair loss and lymphocytic infiltrates in perifollicular and periappendageal regions

shortlist.label: Frontal fibrosing alopecia
shortlist.why_kept: Arc-shaped, depressed skin lesion with localized hair loss on the scalp and forehead, consistent with clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Pseudopelade of Brocq
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic, progressive, asymptomatic, depressed skin lesion with localized hair loss, consistent with clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Fibrosing alopecia in a pattern distribution
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic, progressive, asymptomatic, depressed skin lesion with localized hair loss, consistent with clinical presentation and histopathologic findings

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of linear hair loss, hair thinning, and the presence of short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation on dermoscopic examination are more consistent with lichen planopilaris, a subtype of discoid lupus erythematosus in terms of clinical presentation but distinct in its pathophysiology and treatment approach.

rejected.label: Discoid lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: While the patient's histopathologic examination shows lymphocytic infiltrates and the direct immunofluorescence results are positive, the clinical presentation and dermoscopic findings are more characteristic of lichen planopilaris.

rejected.label: Frontal fibrosing alopecia
rejected.why: The patient's lesions are not limited to the frontal scalp, and the pattern of hair loss is not typical for frontal fibrosing alopecia.

rejected.label: Pseudopelade of Brocq
rejected.why: The presence of significant inflammation and lymphocytic infiltrates on histopathology is not consistent with pseudopelade of Brocq, which is typically characterized by a lack of significant inflammation.

rejected.label: Fibrosing alopecia in a pattern distribution
rejected.why: The patient's hair loss pattern does not follow a typical androgenetic alopecia distribution, and the histopathologic findings are more suggestive of an inflammatory process rather than fibrosing alopecia in a pattern distribution.
